title: Cook white rice in a covered pot
summary: Tender grains with no standing water; about three cups cooked rice from one cup dry, depending on variety.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: 1½–2 cups safe water, following the rice packet when available
Pot with tight lid, heat source, measuring cup, fork

sections.heading: Method
steps: Use the same cup for rice and water. Rinse the rice with safe water if desired; drain well so extra rinse water does not change the ratio.
Put rice and the packet quantity of water in the pot. Bring to a simmer, cover and reduce to the lowest heat that maintains a gentle simmer.
Cook for the packet time, commonly about 15–20 minutes for ordinary white rice. Avoid repeatedly lifting the lid or stirring; both change the steam and starch behaviour.
Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork. Check several grains: they should be tender without a hard centre.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: Tender grains with no standing water; about three cups cooked rice from one cup dry, depending on variety.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Hard grains and dry pot: add 2 tablespoons hot water, cover and cook gently for a few more minutes, then rest.
Wet but tender: uncover briefly over low heat. Burnt bottom: transfer the unburnt top without scraping the base. Adjust heat next time.

sections.heading: Rice types at a glance
steps: These are starting ranges for ordinary dry rice, not quick-cook products. Follow the packet and check doneness; pot, lid, altitude and variety change the result.

cautions: Open the lid away from your face to avoid steam burns.
Cook only what you can eat promptly if reliable refrigeration is unavailable. See the separate rice-leftovers guide.

question_aliases: how to cook white rice in a covered pot

title: Cook brown rice and check the centre
summary: Brown rice stays firmer than white rice; aim for a tender centre, not an identical soft texture.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Water according to packet, often 2–2½ cups for absorption cooking
Lidded pot, low controllable heat, fork

sections.heading: Method
steps: Check that the packet says brown rice; parboiled and quick-cook products have different times. Measure both rice and water with the same cup.
Rinse with safe water and drain. Bring rice and measured water to a boil, then cover and reduce to a gentle simmer.
Begin checking near the packet time, often 35–45 minutes. Sample a cooled grain from the middle: the bran may be chewy, but the centre should not be chalky or hard.
Remove from heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Record your pot, ratio and actual time for the next batch.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: Brown rice stays firmer than white rice; aim for a tender centre, not an identical soft texture.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If the centre is hard after water is absorbed, add a little hot water and continue covered.
If excess water remains but grains are cooked, drain carefully with a heat-safe strainer.

cautions: Rice variety, soaking, altitude and lid fit change water needs. Do not apply white-rice timing to brown rice.
Hot strainers and escaping steam can burn.

question_aliases: how to cook brown rice and check the centre

title: Handle cooked rice leftovers
summary: A dated, rapidly cooled portion with a known cold-storage history.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills

sections.heading: Method
steps: Serve promptly. If keeping rice, divide it into shallow portions rather than leaving a deep warm pot to cool.
Cool rapidly, ideally within one hour, then refrigerate. Do not leave rice on the counter overnight.
Use refrigerated rice within 24 hours. Reheat only once, until steaming hot throughout; stir to remove cold spots.
If time or temperature history is unknown, discard it. Smell does not reliably reveal the hazard.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A dated, rapidly cooled portion with a known cold-storage history.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If electricity fails, record when cooling stopped and consult local food-safety guidance. When safe refrigeration cannot be confirmed, cook fresh portions instead.
Do not try to make neglected rice safe by boiling it again.

cautions: Reheating may not remove toxins formed during poor storage.

title: Cook split red lentils
summary: Soft split lentils that can be mashed; they normally lose their original shape.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: About 3 cups safe water, plus extra if needed

sections.heading: Method
steps: Sort out stones and damaged material. Rinse the lentils in a fine strainer under safe water.
Add water and lentils to a pot with room for foam. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat so the contents simmer without overflowing.
Stir occasionally and check at about 15 minutes. Continue until the lentils mash easily and no hard centre remains; older lentils may need longer.
Add safe hot water for a soup or simmer uncovered for a thicker purée. Season after tasting a cooled spoonful.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: Soft split lentils that can be mashed; they normally lose their original shape.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Foam rising: reduce heat and use a larger pot.
Lentils sticking: add hot water, lower heat and stir the bottom gently.

cautions: This method is for split red lentils, not raw kidney beans, which need different safety preparation.
Store leftovers safely; do not leave a warm pot for prolonged periods.

title: Make porridge from rolled oats
summary: Creamy oats with softened flakes; thickness increases while standing.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: 1 cup safe water or safe milk

sections.heading: Method
steps: Confirm these are rolled oats; steel-cut oats need substantially longer cooking. Measure the oats and liquid.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer, stir in oats and reduce the heat.
Stir regularly for about 5 minutes or the packet time. Keep milk-based porridge below an aggressive boil so it does not scorch.
Rest off heat for 2 minutes, then add small amounts of safe liquid if too thick. Test temperature before serving.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: Creamy oats with softened flakes; thickness increases while standing.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Scorched smell: transfer the upper layer without scraping and use lower heat next time.
Very thin porridge: simmer a little longer while stirring.

cautions: Hot porridge retains heat and can burn the mouth.
Milk requires safe storage; water is preferable if refrigeration is unreliable.

title: Make a simple pan flatbread
summary: Flexible bread with cooked interior and scattered brown spots.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: About ⅓ cup safe water, adding more as needed
Bowl, clean work surface, heavy pan

sections.heading: Method
steps: Mix flour with most of the water. Add the rest gradually until a soft dough forms; flour absorption varies.
Knead briefly until evenly mixed and let the covered dough rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into four portions. Flatten each into a thin disc, about 2–3 mm thick, using a little flour to prevent sticking.
Cook in a hot dry pan, turning when brown spots appear. Cook the second side until the centre has no wet raw dough. Lower heat if the outside burns first.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: Flexible bread with cooked interior and scattered brown spots.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Tearing dough: rest longer and add a little water if dry.
Sticky dough: dust the surface lightly rather than adding large amounts of flour.

cautions: Raw flour is not ready-to-eat food. Cook the centre thoroughly.
Use a stable stove and protect hands from the hot pan.

title: Rotate a dry-food store
summary: A dated store where you can identify the oldest safe stock without opening every container.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills

sections.heading: Method
steps: Record each package, quantity, allergens, opening date and label storage directions. Keep the original label with transferred food.
Inspect for holes, moisture, insects and damaged seals before placing food in the store.
Put the earliest-use packages at the front. Use one open container at a time rather than repeatedly mixing new food with old.
Review weekly during disruption. Set aside suspect food for disposal; never blend it into a sound batch.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A dated store where you can identify the oldest safe stock without opening every container.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Condensation inside a jar means food or the container may have been damp. Do not assume sealing fixes spoilage.
Repeated pests require removing affected food, cleaning shelves and sealing entry points.

cautions: Dry appearance does not make all foods shelf-stable. Follow the product label.
Do not reuse containers that held fuel, pesticide or other non-food chemicals.

title: Prepare familiar purchased fruit safely
summary: A clean portion of a known cultivated food; this is not a plant-identification method.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Fruit from a known food supplier
Clean hands, knife and cutting board

sections.heading: Method
steps: Use fruit you already know as a cultivated food from a reliable supplier. A similar-looking wild fruit is not interchangeable.
Remove visibly rotten or mouldy fruit. Wash hands and rinse the fruit with safe water before cutting, including fruit whose peel will be discarded.
Remove stones, hard seeds or inedible rind according to the known species. Keep the knife from transferring dirt on the peel to the flesh.
Cut only what will be eaten promptly if cold storage is unavailable. Keep cut fruit covered and separate from raw animal foods.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A clean portion of a known cultivated food; this is not a plant-identification method.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If the fruit or species is unfamiliar, retain its label and consult a qualified local source before eating.
Do not remove a bitter or unusual taste merely by adding sugar.

cautions: Never use a universal taste test for wild plants. Some dangerous toxins have no warning taste.
Allergies and individual dietary restrictions still apply.

title: Choose a safe food-drying method
summary: A process record tied to an established recipe, rather than a guessed shelf life.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Clean trays, thermometer, dry storage containers

sections.heading: Method
steps: Select a tested method for the exact food. Fruit, vegetables and meat do not share one safe drying process.
Prepare evenly sized pieces and any specified pretreatment. Load a single layer so air can pass around the pieces.
Use the prescribed temperature and check for the stated dryness endpoint; time alone varies with thickness, humidity and equipment.
Cool and package as directed by the tested method. Label the food and inspect stored batches for moisture or spoilage.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A process record tied to an established recipe, rather than a guessed shelf life.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Uneven drying: reduce piece thickness and avoid crowded trays.
Moisture reappearing in storage means the product was not adequately dried or sealed; follow the tested method rather than simply hiding the wet pieces.

cautions: Do not improvise outdoor drying of meat or vegetables.
Drying does not reliably remove toxins or make an unknown plant edible.

title: Understand why canning recipes cannot be improvised
summary: A decision to use a complete validated process or avoid canning when its requirements cannot be met.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Current tested recipe for the exact food and jar size
Specified canner, jars and altitude adjustment

sections.heading: Method
steps: Identify whether the tested recipe requires a boiling-water canner or pressure canner. Low-acid foods need the specified pressure process.
Match food preparation, jar size, headspace, packing liquid and altitude adjustment exactly.
Write the required pressure or temperature and processing time before starting. If equipment cannot maintain them, choose another safe food-storage method.
After processing, follow the recipe for cooling, seal checks and storage. Keep a batch record so an interrupted process is traceable.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A decision to use a complete validated process or avoid canning when its requirements cannot be met.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: A sealed lid only proves a vacuum formed; it does not prove sufficient heat treatment.
If a process is interrupted, consult the tested instructions for reprocessing limits rather than restarting at a guessed time.

cautions: Never taste suspect canned food. Botulism hazards may not be visible or smell unusual.
Ordinary pressure cookers and small multicookers are not automatically validated pressure canners.

title: Treat microbiologically unsafe water by boiling
summary: Water treated against infectious organisms, provided the original source was not chemically contaminated and it stays clean.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Safe heat source, pot and lid
Clean cloth or filter for visible sediment

sections.heading: Method
steps: Choose the best available source. Reject water suspected of fuel, industrial chemical or radioactive contamination; boiling does not solve those hazards.
Let muddy water settle and pass it through a clean cloth to remove visible particles. This is preparation, not disinfection.
Bring the clear water to a vigorous rolling boil for one minute. Above 6,500 feet (about 2,000 m), use three minutes.
Let it cool in a covered clean vessel. Pour into a clean container without dipping dirty cups or hands into it.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: Water treated against infectious organisms, provided the original source was not chemically contaminated and it stays clean.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If the burner cannot maintain a rolling boil, use another approved treatment or known safe supply.
Recontamination after cooling defeats treatment; clean the lid and dispensing method too.

cautions: Prevent steam burns and keep the pot stable.
Clear-looking water can still contain pathogens; appearance is not a safety test.

title: Store drinking water without recontaminating it
summary: A protected water supply with known origin and handling history.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Food-grade water container with narrow opening and lid

sections.heading: Method
steps: Use a container intended for food or drinking water. Follow local public-health instructions for cleaning and sanitizing it before filling.
Fill with a known safe supply, close the lid and write the filling date and treatment method.
Store away from direct sun, fuel and pesticides. Keep containers off contaminated floors and protect the neck and cap from dirty hands.
Pour water out or use a clean tap; do not dip hands or drinking cups into the supply. Follow local guidance for rotation of stored water.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A protected water supply with known origin and handling history.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: A leaking lid or dirty tap can contaminate otherwise safe water.
If the history is uncertain, use a safe replacement or appropriate treatment for the suspected hazard.

cautions: Never repurpose chemical containers for drinking water.
Storage alone does not disinfect unsafe water.

title: Understand what a portable water filter removes
summary: A treatment process matched to documented filter capabilities.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Filter with readable specifications and intact cartridge

sections.heading: Method
steps: Find the rated contaminant removal, not just the word purifier. A sediment filter is different from a microbial filter, and many filters do not remove viruses or dissolved chemicals.
Inspect seals and cartridge condition. Keep the outlet and clean hose away from untreated water.
Operate within the manufacturer flow and pressure limits. Combine with an approved disinfection step when the filter specification requires it.
Record cartridge use and follow the cleaning or replacement schedule. Protect freeze-sensitive filters from freezing.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A treatment process matched to documented filter capabilities.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Slow flow often means clogging; clean only by the approved method.
Unexpectedly fast flow, cracks or failed seals may mean bypass. Stop using the filter until resolved.

cautions: Improvised sand or cloth filters do not make water microbiologically safe by themselves.
Chemically contaminated water may require a different source, not another pass through the same filter.

title: Understand water distillation and its limits
summary: An understanding of separation by phase change; distillation is not universal decontamination.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Ventilated, stable power and heat arrangement

sections.heading: Method
steps: Distillation evaporates water and condenses the vapour in a separate path. Salts tend to stay in the boiling vessel; some volatile chemicals can travel with the vapour.
Use a purpose-built unit rather than sealing an improvised pressure vessel. Check cooling, seals, clean collection path and allowed feed-water sources.
Operate within the rated fill and heat limits. Keep the product-water vessel separate from the untreated-water vessel.
Allow cooling before cleaning deposits. Record output volume and energy used to judge whether the method is practical for your water needs.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: An understanding of separation by phase change; distillation is not universal decontamination.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Poor condensation wastes vapour; check the approved cooling arrangement.
Unexpected smell or suspected fuel contamination means stop and obtain another source.

cautions: Never seal a heated vessel without engineered pressure protection.
Do not rely on a small solar still as your only emergency water supply.

title: Set up a low-water handwashing station
summary: A station that works without mains plumbing and avoids shared dirty rinse water.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Safe water in a container with tap or pour spout

sections.heading: Method
steps: Place the station near food preparation or toilet access without contaminating either area. Stabilize the water container so it cannot fall.
Wet hands, apply soap and rub all surfaces, including thumbs, between fingers and under nails, for at least 20 seconds.
Rinse with flowing clean water. Collect wastewater so it does not form a muddy pool near the clean supply.
Refill using a clean container and clean the tap regularly. Assign a daily check for soap, water and drainage.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A station that works without mains plumbing and avoids shared dirty rinse water.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If everyone dips hands into one bowl, replace the setup with pouring or a tap.
If water is unsafe, follow local public-health instructions for a suitable handwashing supply.

cautions: Hand sanitizer is not a universal substitute for washing visibly dirty hands.
Keep wastewater away from drinking-water containers and food.

title: Plan a flood escape route before water rises
summary: A route and decision trigger agreed before roads become unsafe.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Local flood information and paper or offline map

sections.heading: Method
steps: Mark higher ground and routes that avoid river crossings, underpasses and low bridges. Identify an alternate route if the usual road closes.
Choose an early departure trigger based on official warnings and your household needs; people with limited mobility need additional time.
Keep keys, medicines, documents and essential supplies ready. Tell a trusted contact the destination when communications are available.
If the route becomes flooded, stop and choose a safe alternative. Follow evacuation instructions and do not enter floodwater to recover belongings.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A route and decision trigger agreed before roads become unsafe.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: A navigation app may show a route without knowing current flood closures. Treat visible water and official barriers as decisive.
If trapped, move to a safer elevated position and signal your location without entering moving water.

cautions: Do not walk, swim or drive through floodwater.
Floodwater may conceal electricity, sewage, debris and washed-out road surfaces.

title: Prepare a room for earthquake shaking
summary: A room with reduced falling-object hazards and a rehearsed protective action.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Furniture anchors appropriate to wall material

sections.heading: Method
steps: Identify sturdy tables or desks away from windows and heavy objects. Practice dropping, covering the head and neck, and holding on.
Move heavy items from high shelves. Secure tall furniture using hardware and installation appropriate for the wall, with help if necessary.
Keep exit paths clear and store shoes and a light where they can be reached after shaking.
After shaking stops, assess injuries and hazards before moving. Expect aftershocks and follow local evacuation advice.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A room with reduced falling-object hazards and a rehearsed protective action.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If no table is nearby, protect the head and neck in a safer interior area away from glass.
Do not spend shaking time trying to cross a room full of falling objects.

cautions: Do not run outdoors during shaking if doing so exposes you to falling debris.
Do not enter visibly damaged structures to retrieve possessions.

title: Stop a navigation mistake from becoming a larger emergency
summary: A documented location uncertainty and deliberate action instead of random wandering.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Offline map, compass and known route
Weather protection, water and signalling equipment

sections.heading: Method
steps: When landmarks no longer match the route, stop in a safe place. Record time and last confirmed location before memory becomes uncertain.
Compare visible terrain with the map without assuming the compass gives a position. Check whether GPS accuracy is adequate for the terrain.
Contact help if possible and report coordinates, map datum if known, injuries and supplies. Keep messages short and conserve power.
Choose a safe waiting place and signal visibly. Move only for a clear safety reason or a route you can justify, leaving a record of the change.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A documented location uncertainty and deliberate action instead of random wandering.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If GPS jumps between distant points, do not chase every reading; wait for a better fix in a safe open area.
Magnetic interference can mislead bearings; step away from vehicles and metal.

cautions: In heat or desert conditions, exertion may rapidly increase water needs.
Do not assume a straight-line bearing is a safe walking route.

title: Prepare a clear distress message
summary: A concise message that helps responders find you and understand the need.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Phone, radio or signalling device you already know how to use

sections.heading: Method
steps: Write your location first: coordinates with hemisphere, or a clear named place and access route. Include the time of the position fix.
State what happened, how many people need help, immediate hazards and urgent medical needs.
Give a callback method and conserve battery after transmitting. Keep the device available for instructions.
If using a radio, follow the service rules and listen before transmitting. Repeat critical numbers slowly and confirm what was received.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A concise message that helps responders find you and understand the need.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If a message fails, try a shorter text where supported and move only to a safer reception point.
If coordinates are uncertain, say so and provide nearby landmarks instead of inventing precision.

A phone cannot connect directly to arbitrary satellites through software alone.

title: Organize the first hour of a power outage
summary: A prioritized response covering safety, communication and essential power.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills

sections.heading: Method
steps: Check for immediate danger such as burning smell, damaged wiring or medical equipment losing power. Seek appropriate help for urgent needs.
Use battery lights and disconnect sensitive equipment when safe. Keep refrigerators and freezers closed while you establish the outage duration.
Check official information through available channels and agree a household meeting or communication plan.
Allocate limited battery power to communication and essential equipment. Record the time cooling and charging stopped.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A prioritized response covering safety, communication and essential power.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If only your property is affected, inspect the labelled breaker panel from a dry safe position without opening covers.
Repeated tripping indicates a fault; do not repeatedly reset or bypass protection.

cautions: Never run a generator, charcoal burner or fuel stove indoors or in a garage.
Do not backfeed a building through a wall socket.

title: Estimate a small battery energy budget
summary: For example, a 5 W light used for 4 hours consumes about 20 Wh before losses.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Device rated voltage and current or power

sections.heading: Method
steps: Use watt-hours when comparing batteries of different voltages. If a battery is labelled amp-hours, multiply nominal volts by amp-hours to estimate watt-hours.
For each load, multiply watts by operating hours. Add the loads to get the planned energy demand.
Allow for conversion losses, standby draw, ageing and temperature. Treat a paper estimate as an upper bound until measured.
Test a short normal-use cycle and record the actual run time. Prioritize essential devices if the measured energy is lower than planned.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: For example, a 5 W light used for 4 hours consumes about 20 Wh before losses.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Milliamp-hour labels cannot be compared directly across different voltages.
A battery that shuts down early may be cold, degraded or overloaded; use its rated limits.

cautions: Do not open, puncture or bypass protection on lithium batteries.
Stop using swollen, hot or damaged packs and follow approved disposal guidance.

title: Diagnose a failed USB charging connection
summary: A fault narrowed to source, cable, connector or device without opening a battery.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills

sections.heading: Method
steps: Check for swelling, heat, liquid or damaged connectors. Stop immediately if any are present.
Try a known working outlet and charger, then change only the cable. Record which single change restores charging.
Inspect the port visually for obstruction without inserting metal tools or liquids. Use only the manufacturer cleaning method.
Restart the device if safe and check whether its charging settings or temperature limits are restricting charging.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A fault narrowed to source, cable, connector or device without opening a battery.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: A cable may carry power but not data, or support only low power. Match the cable and charger ratings.
If charging stops when the cable moves, discontinue that damaged connection.

Do not charge a wet or swollen device.

title: Measure a low-voltage battery with a multimeter
summary: A low-voltage measurement with polarity identified; a negative sign means the probes are reversed.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Known low-voltage battery, such as an AA cell

sections.heading: Method
steps: Read the meter manual. Place black lead in COM and red lead in the voltage socket, not the current socket.
Select DC voltage and a range above the expected battery voltage, or auto-range.
Touch probes to opposite battery terminals without allowing metal probe tips to touch each other. Read the sign and magnitude.
Remove probes and switch the meter off. Compare the result to the battery type and manufacturer guidance; open-circuit voltage does not prove full capacity.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A low-voltage measurement with polarity identified; a negative sign means the probes are reversed.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: An overload indication usually requires a higher voltage range.
A zero reading may mean poor contact, an exhausted battery or an incorrect function; verify on a known safe source.

cautions: Never put a meter in current mode directly across a battery.
This beginner procedure excludes mains, high-energy battery banks and exposed power supplies.

title: Trace an open circuit in a disconnected low-voltage device
summary: A location for a broken connection or switch fault, not a guess based on appearance.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Device with batteries removed and no high-voltage storage

sections.heading: Method
steps: Disconnect all power. Verify the device is a simple low-voltage circuit without capacitors or other stored-energy hazards.
Photograph wiring before moving connectors. Follow the path from battery contact through switch and load.
Use continuity mode only on the unpowered path. Test a short lead first to learn the meter indication.
Check one segment at a time and compare switch-open with switch-closed readings. Reassemble before reconnecting power.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A location for a broken connection or switch fault, not a guess based on appearance.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: Parallel paths can give continuity even when the part under test is open. Consult the diagram and isolate only where safe and documented.
If readings vary when a wire moves, inspect the strain relief and connection.

cautions: Never use resistance or continuity mode on a live circuit.
Do not bypass fuses or safety switches to make the device run.

title: Find and patch a bicycle inner-tube puncture
summary: A tube that holds pressure and a tyre bead seated evenly around the rim.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
prerequisites: Tyre levers, patch kit and pump
Water or careful listening to find leaks

sections.heading: Method
steps: Remove the wheel according to the bicycle instructions, release remaining air and lift one tyre bead with tyre levers.
Remove the tube and inflate it slightly. Find the leak by sound or bubbles, then mark it and dry the tube.
Inspect the matching place inside the tyre for glass or thorns without cutting your fingers. Prepare and apply the patch exactly as the kit specifies.
Slightly inflate the tube, fit it without twisting and reseat the bead. Inflate gradually to the tyre-rated pressure while checking that the tube is not trapped.

sections.heading: Expected result
steps: A tube that holds pressure and a tyre bead seated evenly around the rim.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
steps: If bubbles appear at the patch edge, preparation or curing may have failed.
A split near the valve, large tear or damaged tyre may need replacement rather than patching.

cautions: Check brakes and wheel retention before riding.
Do not exceed tyre or rim pressure limits.

title: Remove and replace a small threaded fastener without damage
summary: A correctly seated fastener with its original hardware order preserved.
audience: Adults learning practical household and preparedness skills
